content: AndroidWeb DevelopmentJavaScriptTechnologySummertimesagaapkEthan ClarkeFollow3 min read·1 day agoListenShareWill My Summertime Saga Save Work After an Update? A Simple Compatibility CheckPress enter or click to view image in full sizePhoto by Franck on UnsplashOne of the most frustrating things about updating Summertime Saga is discovering that your old save doesn't load correctly afterward.If you've spent hours progressing through character routes, unlocking scenes, collecting items, and completing events, starting over is the last thing you want.So before updating, ask:> Will my current Summertime Saga save work with the version I'm installing?That's exactly the problem the SummersagaHub Save Compatibility Checker is designed to help with.Why Save Compatibility MattersA game save isn't just a simple collection of screenshots or progress markers. It contains information created by a particular game version.When the game changes, the way certain data is stored or interpreted can also change.That means you shouldn't automatically assume:Old save + new game version = guaranteed compatibilitySometimes an update works perfectly with an existing save. In other situations, a player may encounter problems such as:A save refusing to loadMissing or unexpected progressCharacters or events behaving differentlyErrors after loading an older saveHaving to start a new game unnecessarilyThe safest approach is to check before making the switch.What Does the SummersagaHub Save Compatibility Checker Do?The Summertime Saga Save Compatibility Checker gives players a quick way to check their save/version combination before updating.Instead of guessing, you can use the checker to determine whether your current save is suitable for the version you want to use.👉 Check your save compatibility:Summertime Saga Save CompatibilityWhen Should You Use It?The checker is particularly useful if you're:Updating to a newer versionBefore replacing your current installation, check your existing save against the version you're moving to.Moving between devicesIf you're transferring your progress from one device to another, checking compatibility first can prevent unnecessary troubleshooting.Returning to the gameMaybe you haven't played Summertime Saga for months and you're using an older installation.Before jumping straight to the newest version, check whether your existing save is suitable.Installing a different buildIf you're switching between different versions, it's better to check first rather than discovering a problem after the change.Get Ethan Clarke’s stories in your inboxJoin Medium for free to get updates from this writer.SubscribeSubscribeRemember me for faster sign inAlways Back Up Your SaveA compatibility checker is useful, but a backup is still essential.Before updating or replacing your game:1. Find your existing save files.2. Copy them to a separate folder.3. Keep that backup somewhere safe.4. Only then install or update the game.5. Test your existing save.If something goes wrong, you still have the original files.Never delete your only copy of a save before testing the new installation.What If Your Save Isn't Compatible?Don't immediately panic.If your save isn't suitable for the version you're moving to, your options depend on the specific situation.You may be better off:Keeping the current game versionRestoring your backupUsing a compatible versionStarting a separate save for the newer versionThe important thing is to know the situation before you overwrite your working installation.A Simple Update ChecklistBefore updating Summertime Saga, run through this checklist:☐ Back up your current save☐ Note the game version you're currently using☐ Check the version you're planning to install☐ Use the SummersagaHub compatibility checker☐ Install the new version separately when possible☐ Test your save before deleting the old installationThis takes much less time than trying to recover lost progress later.Final TipIf you've invested a lot of time into your Summertime Saga save, don't treat an update like a normal app update.Check first. Back up second. Update third.The SummersagaHub Save Compatibility Checker gives you a simple starting point before making that change.👉 Check your Summertime Saga save:Save Compatibility CheckerThis guide is intended as a practical resource for players. title: Moto Pad 70 Launches in India at ₹36,999: 6.29mm Design, 5G and Moto Pen Included
excerpt: Motorola’s new tablet combines a 12.1-inch 2.5K display, 5G connectivity, a 10,200mAh battery and an AI-powered stylus. Continue reading on Medium »
content: TechnologyGadgetsAndroidTabletsMotorolaMoto Pad 70 Launches in India at ₹36,999: 6.29mm Design, 5G and Moto Pen IncludedUnbox Daily HQFollow4 min read·1 day agoListenSharePress enter or click to view image in full sizeMotorola’s new tablet combines a 12.1-inch 2.5K display, 5G connectivity, a 10,200mAh battery and an AI-powered stylus.Motorola has brought the Moto Pad 70 to India at ₹36,999, combining a slim 6.29mm design with 5G connectivity, a 12.1-inch 2.5K display and a large 10,200mAh battery.According to Unbox Daily HQ’s original coverage, the tablet is scheduled to go on sale across India from August 15, 2026. What makes the Moto Pad 70 particularly interesting is that Motorola also includes an AI-powered moto pen with the tablet, giving buyers a more complete productivity and creative setup out of the box.Here’s a closer look at what the new tablet offers.Moto Pad 70: Price and Availability in IndiaThe Moto Pad 70 is priced at ₹36,999 in India, following a 54% reduction from its stated ₹80,000 retail price.Sales across India are scheduled to begin on August 15, 2026.The package also includes a 68W TurboPower charger and cable, so buyers do not need to purchase the charging hardware separately.A Slim 6.29mm Tablet With a 12.1-inch 2.5K DisplayOne of the standout aspects of the Moto Pad 70 is its physical design.The tablet measures 181.8mm wide and 278.8mm high, while the chassis is only 6.29mm thick. At 530 grams, Motorola is positioning it as a portable productivity device.The front is dominated by a 12.1-inch 2.5K display, giving users a relatively large canvas for work, entertainment and creative tasks.The tablet comes in a PANTONE Sea Angel colour finish.5G Connectivity and MediaTek Dimensity 6400Under the hood, the Moto Pad 70 uses a MediaTek Dimensity 6400 processor running at up to 2.5GHz.It is paired with:8GB DDR4X RAM256GB internal storage5G connectivityWi-FiSingle SIM supportBluetooth 5.2 EDRThe tablet also supports standard voice calling, making its cellular connectivity more useful than a Wi-Fi-only tablet.The Moto Pen Comes in the BoxPerhaps the most interesting part of the package is the included AI-powered moto pen.Rather than requiring buyers to purchase a stylus separately, Motorola includes it with the tablet.The pen supports:4,096 pressure levelsTilt detectionPalm rejectionThat makes the Moto Pad 70 particularly relevant for users who want to take handwritten notes, sketch or work with digital artwork.An optional Moto Folio keyboard can also be attached through magnetic pogo-pin connectors.10,200mAh Battery and 68W ChargingThe Moto Pad 70 packs a substantial 10,200mAh battery, designed to support longer sessions of media consumption and productivity.Charging is handled through the included 68W TurboPower charger, connected through USB Type-C.The combination of a large battery and fast charging gives the tablet a useful advantage for people who expect to use it away from a desk.Get Unbox Daily HQ’s stories in your inboxJoin Medium for free to get updates from this writer.SubscribeSubscribeRemember me for faster sign inMoto Pad 70 Specifications at a GlanceDisplay 12.1-inch 2.5KProcessor MediaTek Dimensity 6400RAM 8GB DDR4XStorage 256GBRear Camera 13MPBattery 10,200mAhCharging 68W TurboPowerStorage Can Be ExpandedThe tablet includes a dedicated microSD slot, allowing storage to be expanded up to 2TB.That could be particularly useful for users who keep large collections of documents, photos, videos or other files locally.Software SupportThe Moto Pad 70 runs Android 16, with an upgrade to Android 18 guaranteed according to the original launch information.Motorola also lists security patches through 2030, giving the tablet a longer software-support window.Smart Connect for Multi-Device UseMotorola’s Smart Connect framework enables multi-device connectivity.For users already working across multiple devices, this can make the tablet more useful as part of a broader digital setup rather than simply functioning as a standalone screen.Camera and Other HardwareThe rear camera is rated at 13MP.The tablet also includes several sensors:AccelerometerAmbient light sensorHall sensorThe retail box contains the tablet, moto pen, charger, cable, tray pin and safety documentation.Why It MattersThe Moto Pad 70’s biggest selling point isn’t simply its display or processor. It is the combination of hardware and accessories included at ₹36,999.The 6.29mm body, 5G connectivity, 10,200mAh battery and 2.5K display make it suitable for mobile productivity, while the included 4,096-level pressure-sensitive moto pen adds value for note-taking and creative work.For buyers comparing tablets at this price level, not having to purchase a compatible stylus separately can make the overall package more attractive.Our TakeThe Moto Pad 70 appears particularly well suited to students, working professionals and digital creators who want one portable device for multiple tasks.Its strongest proposition is the complete package: a large 2.5K screen, 5G, substantial battery, expandable storage and a capable stylus included in the box.The 530g weight and 6.29mm thickness also help it remain practical for people who regularly move between home, college, office or other locations.At ₹36,999, the Moto Pad 70 is therefore less about being a basic media tablet and more about providing a portable productivity setup without requiring several additional purchases.The Moto Pad 70 arrives in India at ₹36,999, bringing together a slim 6.29mm design, 12.1-inch 2.5K display, MediaTek Dimensity 6400 processor, 5G connectivity and a 10,200mAh battery.The included AI-powered moto pen is arguably the most notable part of the package, especially for students and creators who want stylus functionality from day one.Retail sales are scheduled to start across India on August 15, 2026.For the complete launch details and the latest information, read the original Moto Pad 70 article on Unbox Daily HQ.Source: Original article on Unbox

title: From Wear to Pebble
excerpt: I have moved off of Wear OS and onto a Pebble watch!
content: From Wear to Pebble Initially, when wearables debuted, I was dubious. I had little doubt that some people would find them to be useful, but I did not expect that I would be among them. Then, around late 2020, my team at MIRROR needed to add Android Wear/Wear OS support to our fitness mirror. So, I bought a few Wear devices for testing. I quickly determined that Wear 2 devices were less than completely useful, with CPUs that reminded me of Android phones from 2009 coupled with an OS that needed more than that. But, the Samsung Watch with Wear OS 3 was nice, and I took to it as a “daily driver” wearable. Over the years, I moved from that Samsung to a Mobvoi TicWatch, then later to a Pixel Watch 3. Increasingly, I found Wear OS to be annoying, but I stuck with it. More recently, after a botched attempt to move my daily driver phone to GrapheneOS, I lost a lot of watch functionality, as I could never get it re-connected fully to my pre-GrapheneOS phone. 🤷🏻 When rePebble appeared on the scene last year, I took notice. I had never owned a Pebble, but I remembered their Kickstarter era. Plus, the TicWatch used an eInk/e-paper screen for its always-on experience (dual-layered with a classic touchscreen), and I appreciated the low power draw. So, I took the plunge and bought a Pebble Time 2. A few weeks later, my Pixel Watch 3 is up for sale on eBay. Is Pebble OS as powerful as Wear OS? No. Is the Time 2 as powerful as the Pixel Watch 3? Ha ha ha ha ha ha… no. But I don’t really need that kind of power, which mostly seemed to be there to make for snazzy animations, even if the underlying apps were less than completely stable. 🧐 What I wanted was something that was less-Googly, required fewer charges, had an open source foundation, and had a developer ecosystem. The Pebble qualifies on all those fronts. I’ll be writing some Pebble apps and contributing to others. I am not going to turn this into a Pebble blog 😅, but I’ll mention my Pebble work from time to time. After nearly 20 years of freelance developer advocacy for Android, between Pebble and my Kotlin Multiplatform projects, it’s kinda nice to be thinking about different platforms for some stuff. — Aug 08, 2026
